SqlAuthenticationProvider.summary: Defines the core behavior of authentication providers and provides a base class for derived classes.
SqlAuthenticationProvider.remarks: Derived classes must provide a parameterless constructor if they can be instantiated from the app.config file.

BeforeLoad.summary: This method is called immediately before the provider is added to the SQL authentication provider registry.
BeforeLoad.remarks:
This callback runs outside the registry lookup/publication lock. It delays the calling registration, not other lookups. Concurrent or reentrant registration changes can cause callbacks to be retried.
This method must not throw.

BeforeUnload.summary: This method is called immediately before the provider is removed from the SQL authentication provider registry.
BeforeUnload.remarks:
This method is called when a different provider replaces this provider for the same method. It runs outside the lookup/publication lock; lookups retain the existing provider until successful publication. Concurrent or reentrant registration changes can cause retries.
This method must not throw.

IsSupported.summary: Indicates whether the specified authentication method is supported.
IsSupported.returns: if the specified authentication method is supported; otherwise, .

AcquireTokenAsync.summary: Acquires an access token from the authority.
AcquireTokenAsync.param: The parameters passed to the provider by the driver.
AcquireTokenAsync.remarks: During federated authentication, the driver passes the server-supplied STSURL and SPN as and , respectively. These values reflect the server's authentication configuration; the provider uses them according to its token acquisition requirements.
AcquireTokenAsync.returns: Represents an asynchronous operation that returns the AD authentication token.

GetProvider.summary: Gets an authentication provider by method.
GetProvider.returns: The authentication provider or if no provider is registered.
GetProvider.remarks:
Bootstraps the registry on first access. Explicit registration in trimmed and NativeAOT applications requires disabling configuration and Azure discovery at publish time. Trimmed JIT apps may retain enabled reflective paths when they preserve the configuration infrastructure, handlers, initializer/provider types and discovered Azure contracts. Enabled paths report trimming and dynamic-code warnings as applicable. Recoverable registry initialization failures emit diagnostic traces through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource with the Trace keyword (0x2). Enable tracing before the first registry access to capture configuration-reading, initializer/provider activation and Azure-discovery failures. Recoverable failures in these steps are traced. Activation failures retain their original exceptions. A failed explicit method returns null instead of an earlier provider or Azure default. Failed initializers block defaults for otherwise-unregistered methods. Subsequent lookups of affected methods trace their retained activation failures. Unexpected recoverable bootstrap failures are also cached and logged on later accesses. Unaffected successfully registered providers remain usable. Register an application provider as a workaround, or correct the reported configuration or package version problem and restart the application to retry bootstrap.
User callbacks execute outside the lookup/publication lock. Concurrent or reentrant registration changes cause replacement to recheck precedence and retry callbacks. During bootstrap, concurrent and reentrant lookups see only providers published so far; a method not initialized yet can return null. During replacement, lookups retain the previous provider until successful publication.

SetProvider.summary: Sets an authentication provider by method.
SetProvider.returns: if the operation succeeded; otherwise, (for example, the existing provider disallows overriding).
SetProvider.remarks:
Works directly under NativeAOT when reflective bootstrap is disabled at publish time. Successfully registered configuration providers and configured initializers cannot be overwritten by application registrations. Application registrations replace the discovered Azure default. Outside configured initializer execution, a null provider, unsupported method or recoverable provider callback failure returns false and emits diagnostic traces through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource with the Trace keyword (0x2). During a configured initializer, registration errors propagate to the configuration application step and stop that initializer. Recoverable initializer failures are traced, and later configured providers are still attempted. Failed explicit methods cannot use earlier providers or defaults. Failed initializers prevent defaults for unknown intended methods. Application registration can explicitly recover a failed method. Fatal failures propagate, including failures nested in inner or aggregate exceptions. Fatal bootstrap failures are not cached; later access can retry bootstrap and repeat earlier side effects if execution continues. Failed application registrations do not publish the candidate provider. Unexpected recoverable bootstrap failures are cached and traced, but application registration remains available without retrying bootstrap. Existing configuration registrations retain precedence. Correct the reported cause and restart the application to retry failed configuration or discovery.
User callbacks execute outside the lookup/publication lock. Concurrent or reentrant changes cause replacement to recheck precedence and retry callbacks. Only registrations on the configured initializer's own thread inherit configuration precedence and propagate registration errors to the initializer. This compares managed thread IDs while Initialize is running; it does not track logical async context. Queued work or continuations on another thread use application precedence and return false on recoverable registration errors, even if the initializer waits for that work. The marker is cleared when Initialize returns or throws; asynchronous work is not awaited. GetProvider does not use this thread-ID check. Concurrent bootstrap access observes published state without waiting for initialization to finish; later configuration registrations can replace application registrations made during bootstrap.
